title: Shepherd's Pie with Cheesy Mash
subtitle: savoury beef, carrot & corn filling in a rich gravy, under a golden cheddar mashed-potato lid
imageAlt: Shepherd's pie with a browned cheddar mashed potato top and a scoop showing beef, carrot and corn filling
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 3–4 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Frozen beef? Thaw in the fridge overnight.
Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Use a 9×13 in or 3 L baking dish.
Get the potatoes boiling first — they take the longest.
Strictly speaking, beef makes this a 'cottage pie' — in Canada most people call it shepherd's pie either way.

steps.title: Boil the potatoes
steps.text: Cover the potatoes with cold water in a big pot, add the salt and bring to a boil. Simmer 15–18 minutes until a knife slides in with no resistance.

steps.title: Brown the beef
steps.text: Meanwhile heat the oil in a large oven-safe skillet or pot over medium-high. Cook the beef, breaking it up, 7–8 minutes until browned with no pink (71°C / 160°F). Drain off extra fat.

steps.title: Soften the veg
steps.text: Add the onion and carrots and cook 5 minutes until softened. Stir in the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute, then sprinkle over the flour and stir 1 minute more.

steps.title: Make the gravy
steps.text: Stir in the broth, Worcestershire, thyme, salt and pepper. Simmer 5 minutes until thick and glossy, then stir in the frozen corn. Taste and adjust the salt. Spread into the baking dish (or leave it in an oven-safe skillet).

steps.title: Mash with cheese
steps.text: Drain the potatoes well and let them steam dry 1 minute. Mash with the butter, warm milk, 1 cup of the cheddar, garlic powder and salt until smooth and fluffy.

steps.title: Top and bake
steps.text: Spoon the mash over the filling, starting at the edges to seal it, and rough up the top with a fork (the ridges get crispy). Scatter the last ½ cup cheddar on top. Bake at 200°C (400°F) 20–25 minutes until bubbling at the edges and golden. Rest 10 minutes before serving.

fixIt.fix: Simmer the gravy a few minutes longer before topping, and rest the pie 10 minutes after baking.
Let the filling cool for 5 minutes and spoon the mash on in dollops from the edges in, rather than dumping it in the middle.
Broil 2–3 minutes at the end — watch it closely.
Don't use a blender or overwork the potatoes; mash by hand while hot.

saleTip: A 4.54 kg (10 lb) bag of potatoes at No Frills is often under $5 in fall — far cheaper per kilo than the small bags.
swap: Ground turkey or lamb (lamb makes it a true shepherd's pie). Swap corn for frozen peas & carrots if you like them.
leftovers: Fridge 4 days. Freezes well (whole or portions) for up to 3 months.
source: Based on tested cottage/shepherd's pie methods (RecipeTin Eats, Allrecipes): browned beef in a broth-and-tomato-paste gravy, thick mashed potato top baked at 200°C.
prepAhead: Make the filling up to 2 days ahead and refrigerate.
Assemble the whole pie a day ahead; bake from cold 35–40 minutes.
Freeze assembled (unbaked) up to 3 months; thaw overnight in the fridge before baking.
reheat: Microwave a portion covered 2–3 minutes until 74°C (165°F), or oven 180°C (350°F) covered 20 min (uncover the last 5).

basic.note: Beef, onion and gravy under plain buttery mash — no cheese crust, fewer jars to open.

stepNotes.3: Basic: skip the Worcestershire and corn — add an extra pinch of salt.
stepNotes.4: Basic: mash with butter, milk and salt.
stepNotes.5: Basic: no cheese on top — brush with a little melted butter for colour.

fancy.note: Golden piped-style mash with aged cheddar and a crisp Parmesan crust, peas instead of corn and a richer gravy.

items.name: egg yolk
items.note: beaten into the mash for a golden crust

stepNotes.3: Fancy: stir a tablespoon of butter into the gravy at the end for shine.
stepNotes.4: Fancy: beat the egg yolk into the mash last.

addSteps.title: Fancy crust
addSteps.text: Pipe or swirl the mash in tight peaks with the back of a spoon, scatter the Parmesan over the cheddar and bake as written. Broil 1–2 minutes at the end until the peaks are deep golden. Rest 10 minutes so it slices cleanly.

plating: Rest 10 minutes, then cut a clean square with a hot wet knife.
Serve in a shallow bowl so the gravy pools at the side.
A crack of black pepper over the golden peaks.

why.1-5: Tomato paste deepens the gravy colour and flavour. Skip it and the filling is paler and milder.
why.1-6: Flour thickens the gravy. Without it the filling is soupy under the mash.
why.1-8: Worcestershire adds the savoury, slightly tangy depth. Skip it and add a little extra salt.
why.0-2: Butter makes the mash silky. Less butter = a stiffer, drier topping.

funFact: Strictly speaking, shepherd’s pie is made with lamb (shepherds look after sheep). Made with beef, it’s traditionally called cottage pie, a name in use since the late 1700s.

keeps.note: whole or in portions, wrapped well
